admission.justification: Three handlings of frozen omissions were weighed with real-data evidence; every later landing, readback and validation must obey the chosen handling.

alternatives.option: Keep frozen rows byte-identical with both facts missing, and read them back as effect not recorded and own revision not recorded.
alternatives.reason: The rows were judged when their leaves published them or predate the rule; freezing is what makes earlier attempts auditable.

alternatives.option: Backfill a default, empty string, zero, current revision or member-derived label and revision onto the old rows.
alternatives.reason: Backfill invents judgments no curator made and rewrites frozen bytes; the packet forbids every one of these fill-ins.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A migration is explicitly requested that re-judges rather than fills, with its own packet and evidence.

alternatives.option: Report the missing facts as a measured absence or a failure of the old rows.
alternatives.reason: A missing key on a frozen row is a recorded omission, not a failed write; absence claims would refuse landings that the rule must pass.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The readback stops distinguishing recorded omission from failed writes.

consequences: The four listed history blobs stay identical across the leaf.
Index, timeline and public reads carry the missing keys missing, never a default.
Edits and deletions of frozen rows still fail the frozen-history check.
context: Sixteen family rows over four history files predate the rule with neither effect nor own revision; the master landing carries them onto the sprint line.
decider: Requirement packet MIK-R48@v2, rules 3 and 5 with Expected Evidence.

evidence: scratch/l48_realdata_driver.out: first run 209 R22.6-anchor-path with 0 R48, corrected run LANDING-PROBE None plus 16/9/5/2 census
